article.title: GE Aerospace and NASA Fly Hybrid-Electric Propulsion Above 30,000 Feet in World-First Demonstration
article.summary: GE Aerospace, NASA, BETA Technologies, and Boeing flew a hybrid-electric propulsion system above 30,000 feet on a modified Saab 340B, unveiled at the Farnborough Airshow.
article.body_markdown:
## Overview

GE Aerospace announced on July 20 at the Farnborough International Airshow in England that it has flown a hybrid-electric propulsion system above 30,000 feet, the altitude band used by commercial passenger jets, a milestone the company and NASA each independently describe as a first for the industry, according to [GE Aerospace](https://www.geaerospace.com/news/press-releases/ge-aerospace-partners-nasa-beta-technologies-and-boeing-worlds-first-high-altitude) and [NASA](https://www.nasa.gov/directorates/rtmd/nasa-ge-hybrid-electric-flight/). The demonstration, conducted with NASA, BETA Technologies, and Boeing, used a modified Saab 340B testbed nicknamed "Gertrude," and the single longest flight in hybrid-electric operation exceeded two hours, according to [GE Aerospace](https://www.geaerospace.com/news/press-releases/ge-aerospace-partners-nasa-beta-technologies-and-boeing-worlds-first-high-altitude).

## What We Know

**The aircraft and its systems.** The right side of the Saab 340B was modified with a hybrid-electric propulsion system fitted inside an inverted nacelle, while the left side retained a standard GE CT7 turboprop, according to [GE Aerospace](https://www.geaerospace.com/news/press-releases/ge-aerospace-partners-nasa-beta-technologies-and-boeing-worlds-first-high-altitude) and [Aviation Week](https://aviationweek.com/aerospace/emerging-technologies/ge-aerospace-marks-hybrid-electric-first-saab-340b). The hybrid-electric system incorporates GE Aerospace-developed motor/generators, power converters, inverters, controllers, Avio Aero gearboxes, Dowty propellers, and Unison heat exchangers, with batteries supplied by BAE Systems and the electrified nacelle supplied by Boeing subsidiary Aurora Flight Sciences, according to [GE Aerospace](https://www.geaerospace.com/news/press-releases/ge-aerospace-partners-nasa-beta-technologies-and-boeing-worlds-first-high-altitude) and [Aviation Business News](https://www.aviationbusinessnews.com/farnborough-international-airshow-2026/ge-aerospace-demonstrates-hybrid-electric-flight-above-30000ft/). A Saab 340B typically seats 30 to 36 passengers, according to [Aerospace America](https://aerospaceamerica.aiaa.org/ge-beta-collaborate-on-first-hybrid-electric-flight-above-30000-feet/).

**A years-long federal program.** The propulsion system was developed through NASA's Electrified Powertrain Flight Demonstration (EPFD) project, for which GE Aerospace received a $179 million contract in 2021, according to [Aerospace America](https://aerospaceamerica.aiaa.org/ge-beta-collaborate-on-first-hybrid-electric-flight-above-30000-feet/). NASA said the work also drew on its ongoing Subsonic Vehicle Technologies and Tools project. Ralph Jansen, an aerospace engineer at NASA's Glenn Research Center, called it "the culmination of more than 15 years of work," according to [NASA](https://www.nasa.gov/directorates/rtmd/nasa-ge-hybrid-electric-flight/). Laurie Grindle, director of the Aeronautics Division within NASA's Research and Technology Mission Directorate, said the achievement "reflects what NASA does best in aeronautics: we explore bold possibilities, validate them through rigorous research and testing, and work with industry to turn breakthrough ideas into technologies that bring real value for the American people," according to [NASA](https://www.nasa.gov/directorates/rtmd/nasa-ge-hybrid-electric-flight/).

**How the flight tests unfolded.** GE Aerospace first flew the aircraft on May 3, and reached the milestone altitude — flying above 30,000 feet over Vermont — on May 20, according to [FlightGlobal](https://www.flightglobal.com/archive/2026/07/ge-aerospace-flies-high-altitude-high-voltage-flight-with-hybrid-electric-saab-340/) and [Aviation Week](https://aviationweek.com/aerospace/emerging-technologies/ge-aerospace-marks-hybrid-electric-first-saab-340b). Christine Andrews, GE Aerospace's hybrid-electric leader, said the flight-test campaign "was wildly successful," and that by May 20 "we were able to operate the hybrid system in flight on the Saab 340 at over 30,000 feet altitude, both motored and generated at full power," using the system "to get to a higher altitude than what the Saab is rated for or can go to on its own CT7 power and sustain that for two hours," according to [Aviation Week](https://aviationweek.com/aerospace/emerging-technologies/ge-aerospace-marks-hybrid-electric-first-saab-340b). Ground testing had previously simulated conditions up to 45,000 feet at NASA's Electric Aircraft Testbed at the Neil A. Armstrong Test Facility in Sandusky, Ohio, in 2022, according to [NASA](https://www.nasa.gov/directorates/rtmd/nasa-ge-hybrid-electric-flight/) and [GE Aerospace](https://www.geaerospace.com/news/press-releases/ge-aerospace-partners-nasa-beta-technologies-and-boeing-worlds-first-high-altitude).

**The transatlantic ferry.** BETA Technologies served as systems integrator, with its pilots flying the aircraft from BETA's flight-test site in Plattsburgh, New York, to the airshow via Goose Bay, Canada; Nuuk, Greenland; Keflavik, Iceland; and Wick, Scotland, before staging at Bournemouth, according to [Aviation Week](https://aviationweek.com/aerospace/emerging-technologies/ge-aerospace-marks-hybrid-electric-first-saab-340b). The aircraft departed Plattsburgh on June 26 and arrived at Farnborough on July 14, according to [FlightGlobal](https://www.flightglobal.com/archive/2026/07/ge-aerospace-flies-high-altitude-high-voltage-flight-with-hybrid-electric-saab-340/). The hybrid-electric system was engaged during each leg of the journey, according to [GE Aerospace](https://www.geaerospace.com/news/press-releases/ge-aerospace-partners-nasa-beta-technologies-and-boeing-worlds-first-high-altitude).

**What the power levels mean.** Arjan Hegeman, GE Aerospace's vice president of future flight engineering, said the demonstration involved "effectively the equivalent of three CT7 engines instead of just two," calling the "really high voltage, massive wattage power in that motor generator at altitude...really a first," according to [Aviation Week](https://aviationweek.com/aerospace/emerging-technologies/ge-aerospace-marks-hybrid-electric-first-saab-340b). GE Aerospace Chairman and CEO H. Lawrence Culp Jr. called it "one for the history books," according to [GE Aerospace](https://www.geaerospace.com/news/press-releases/ge-aerospace-partners-nasa-beta-technologies-and-boeing-worlds-first-high-altitude) and [Aviation Business News](https://www.aviationbusinessnews.com/farnborough-international-airshow-2026/ge-aerospace-demonstrates-hybrid-electric-flight-above-30000ft/), while BETA Founder and CEO Kyle Clark said the campaign created "a flying laboratory to inform all future hybrid designs," according to [GE Aerospace](https://www.geaerospace.com/news/press-releases/ge-aerospace-partners-nasa-beta-technologies-and-boeing-worlds-first-high-altitude). NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman, speaking at Farnborough, said the agency was "moving out of the lab and into practical application," according to [Aviation Week](https://aviationweek.com/aerospace/emerging-technologies/ge-aerospace-marks-hybrid-electric-first-saab-340b).

## What We Don't Know

GE Aerospace has not disclosed a timeline for when hybrid-electric propulsion might reach commercial airline service. Hegeman said the power and voltage levels demonstrated "are unlikely to be the first step in a narrowbody platform," with the testbed's lessons instead set to inform the Open Fan engine architecture under development through GE's CFM International RISE program with joint-venture partner Safran, according to [Aviation Week](https://aviationweek.com/aerospace/emerging-technologies/ge-aerospace-marks-hybrid-electric-first-saab-340b). Andrews said the team still has "a few more things we want to do" and "a few events" planned for the testbed "before we determine its end fate," according to [Aviation Week](https://aviationweek.com/aerospace/emerging-technologies/ge-aerospace-marks-hybrid-electric-first-saab-340b), leaving the aircraft's future beyond this year's airshow circuit unresolved. Neither GE Aerospace nor NASA has disclosed the total cost of the EPFD flight-test campaign beyond the initial $179 million contract award.
